title: Information Retrieval and Search Engines
content: Information retrieval is the science of searching for information in documents. Search engines like Google use inverted indexes to map terms to documents efficiently. The TF-IDF weighting scheme measures term importance by combining term frequency and inverse document frequency. Cosine similarity compares document vectors to rank search results by relevance. Boolean retrieval models use AND OR NOT operators to filter documents. Modern search engines also use PageRank link analysis and machine learning for ranking.
